newsitem.title: UK: Egypt unlikely to buy wheat soon - Shakankiri.
newsitem.headline: Egypt unlikely to buy wheat soon - Shakankiri.

text.p: Egypt is unlikely to tap world wheat markets soon as it enjoys comfortable supplies, the chairman of state procurement agency GASC said on Thursday.

"I am very relaxed. We are starting the new season with large stocks. We are in a very strong position to face the market," Ahmed Samir el Shakankiri told a reporter during a London meeting of the International Grains Council.
"Of course, world prices are falling but we can afford to wait for them to drop further," he added.

Shakankiri said that Egypt was expected to harvest around six million tonnes of wheat in 1997 and that his agency was confident it could achieve its target of securing two million tonnes out of that crop.
"As of Monday, I have received already one million tonnes. We can easily achieve an extra one million," he said. - - London Newsroom +44 171 542 7729
